## Welcome {.unnumbered}

## What You Will Learn {.unnumbered}

The book progresses through six structural parts grounded in the Stochastic Computer architecture, followed by a capstone synthesis:

- **The Stochastic Processor** develops the foundation model as a neural execution core (ALU), analyzing decoding dynamics under memory bandwidth limits, grammar-constrained logit masking, and test-time deliberation algorithms that scale inference compute.
- **Context Memory & Storage** establishes the memory hierarchy of agentic systems, from L1 active attention working sets and compaction, to L2 paged virtual memory (PagedAttention) and Radix prefix sharing, to L3 episodic retrieval stores.
- **Tool Actuation & I/O Peripherals** develops the interface between neural logits and deterministic environments, covering typed communication protocols (Model Context Protocol), actuation idempotency contracts, and hardware-virtualized sandboxing (microVMs, Wasm, Copy-on-Write filesystems).
- **The Agent Operating System** treats the runtime executive that keeps long-running trajectories dependable, including state checkpointing with distributed Sagas, asynchronous interrupt handling for human-in-the-loop preemption, and multi-tenant trajectory scheduling.
- **The Policy Compiler** examines how empirical runtime execution traces are compiled back into model weights via synthetic data flywheels, masked supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning with verifiable reward environments (RLVR / GRPO).
- **The Distributed Fleet** scales agent systems to clusters of cooperating entities, investigating multi-agent topologies and consensus, distributed OpenTelemetry trajectory tracing, and the macro-tokenomics of accelerator fleet sizing.
- **Capstone Synthesis** synthesizes the timeless systems invariants of autonomous runtimes, traces the transition to embodied physical robotics, and maps the grand open challenges of long-horizon autonomous computing.
